title: LLSVP spatial-filter hypothesis: has global seismicity been correlated with LLSVP geometry and CMB heat-flux heterogeneity (KN-5.3 test) - evidence audit for OTA-SCI-0043
question: Source-grounded audit of the [H]/[S]-marked spatial-filter claims in OTA-SCI-0043-2026-DE that LLSVPs create zones of reduced CMB heat flux and thereby spatially filter core-mantle coupling, LOD periodicities (Dumont et al. 2025) and regional seismicity. The curator's [KN-5.3] note asserts: 'Seismizitätsraten geographisch aufgelöst gegen LLSVP-Projektionen auf die Oberfläche korrelieren. Die Daten existieren. Niemand hat es gemacht.' (a) As of 2026, is this still accurate - has any published study correlated spatially resolved global seismicity (including deep-focus and intermediate-depth earthquakes) with LLSVP surface projections, LLSVP margins, or CMB heat-flux heterogeneity, and what do such studies report (supporting, null or constraining evidence)? (b) What do existing deep-earthquake distributions show relative to LLSVP geometry - e.g. do the Pacific subduction rings, the western Pacific deep-focus cluster, or intraplate seismicity fall preferentially along LLSVP margins, and is there any documented seismicity-rate enhancement near plume-root regions of the African/Pacific LLSVPs? (c) For the related claim that LLSVPs act as a spatial filter on core-mantle coupling modes (6-year LOD cycle / torsional Alfvén waves; Dumont periodicities ~90% variance), what supporting or constraining evidence exists that CMB heat-flux heterogeneity is spatially organized by LLSVP geometry and that this modulates LOD/seismicity signals? (d) Is the South Atlantic Anomaly region (produced by the African LLSVP's field-intensity reduction) associated with any distinct regional seismicity signal that could serve as the proposed test case, and what is the current state of evidence for the African LLSVP-SAA causal link itself? Map supporting, null and constraining evidence without upgrading the [H] spatial-filter claim to established; explicitly preserve it as untested if the literature confirms the curator's 'nobody has done it' claim. Do NOT research the AVI [S] layer (Section VII) or validate fictional/Ommizedenz framework claims.
why_now: Section V.3 and the document's 'Nächste Schritte' list explicitly identify the geographical correlation test (seismicity rates vs. LLSVP projections) as the archive's highest-priority open empirical test for the LLSVP spatial-filter hypothesis. The document was drafted 2026-02-09, and a targeted literature check can determine whether recent deep-Earth seismology or geodynamic work has since tested or constrained the hypothesis - which directly determines whether OTA-SCI-0043's [HYPOTHETICAL] status for 'LLSVPs modulieren regionale Seismizität' should be retained, upgraded or narrowed, and whether a real-science contribution is warranted.
real_world_anchor: Testable hypothesis: spatial correlation between global seismicity rates and LLSVP surface projections / CMB heat-flux heterogeneity (KN-5.3); supporting evidence base: deep-focus earthquake distributions, Dumont et al. (2025) planetary-forcing-LOD-seismicity periodicities, and the African LLSVP - South Atlantic Anomaly causal link.
novelty_reason: Prior topic RES-20260829-A464A32B verified the Dumont et al. (2025) planetary-forcing claims in OTA-SCI-0042 but did not address the spatial dimension introduced in OTA-SCI-0043 - whether LLSVP geometry modulates those periodicities and regional seismicity. This gap tests the materially unresolved KN-5.3 spatial-correlation hypothesis and its supporting/constraining literature, which is a distinct claim in a distinct source document.
